why: phase-515 R10 stage 1b (2026-10-27): the executor's node-id-keyed parameter forms left the Rust user surface (behind the sealed `nros_node::executor::ffi::ExecutorFfi`, as R9 stage 1 did for the C-shaped entry points), so the node is the one user-facing parameter receiver, as rclrs's is. `Node::argv_param_overrides` forwards to `Executor::argv_param_overrides_on(node_id, ...)`; the store is still the executor's one table (phase-426 W1). rclrs's `Node` has none; the counterpart is rclcpp's `NodeParametersInterface::get_parameter_overrides()`. PRIOR ROW (`rust:Executor::argv_param_overrides_on`): issue 2057 -- the store-side reader behind rclcpp's `NodeParametersInterface::get_parameter_overrides()`, which the C++ shim forwards to. Upstream keeps a node's `-p` / `--params-file` overrides in the node's own `NodeParameters` and returns them from there; ours keeps them in the executor's one parameter store (see `rust:Executor::allow_undeclared_parameters_on`), so the reader is on the executor and the node is an ARGUMENT. It selects as a declaration does: the last override of a name wins and a `node:` override applies only to that node. A listing has no declared type, so each text is typed bool, integer, double, then string, and an override no type accepts is left out. Test: `packages/core/nros-node/src/executor/tests.rs` (`the_node_carries_the_whole_parameter_surface`).
